fact: University of Botswana researchers used CHIRPS satellite rainfall and CHIRTS satellite-derived temperature data (25 km) to compute drought indices and test them against national crop-yield data for agricultural drought monitoring in Botswana.

University of Botswana researchers used CHIRPS satellite rainfall estimates (1981-2024, 25 km) to regionalise Botswana into drought zones and recommended building Nino 3.4 and SOI indices into national drought forecasting and early-warning systems.

Digital Earth Africa and SASSCAL agreed to build the AgriWatch dashboard on DE Africa Earth-observation products for crop-cycle, rangeland and rainfall monitoring, with AgriWatch covering this country among the six SASSCAL states.
